content.text:
**Finding submitted — EXCLUSIVITY: deviation (walk-away territory), preferred cure proposed.**

- **Responsive clause:** Section 6.1 (p0037) — the Company may not participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products "during the term of this Agreement," and HDI takes "the exclusive right to use of the 'Deerskin' brand" for a direct-to-consumer site.
- **Why it fails fallback:** the term is one year auto-renewing on each anniversary (§4.1), so exclusivity is open-ended rather than capped at 12 months; there is no automatic termination on service-level or delivery-date failure (§1.6 gives only a discretionary termination right if the Site is not live within 70 days); §6.2's closeout carve-out does not time-box or exit-link the covenant. HDI also holds an exclusive right over our own brand, which independently defeats the preferred "no field-of-use restriction" test.
- **Cure:** a single surgical replace of the offending covenant with "The Company shall have no exclusivity, non-compete or sole-supplier obligation under this Agreement, and HDI shall have no exclusive right to use the 'Deerskin' brand." §6.2 (our retained closeout rights) and §6.3 (HDI's reciprocal restriction, which benefits us) are preserved verbatim; the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic performance-based exit) is offered in the comment.
